At the [previous discussion](https://github.com/YannJY02/InvisibleResearch/blob/main/meeting-reports/2026-10-22-predictor-decisions-and-encoding.md), we agreed to retain potentially useful information and check what these fields mean before choosing numeric features.

## 1. What does the agreed set of 40 fields contain?

**Answer:** It contains **38 candidate predictor fields and two Scopus outcome fields**, not 40 model features. The frozen dataset contains 207,602 sources and 80 columns. This report checks those data without changing the agreed labels or fitting a model.


```{r}
#| label: frozen-input
library(data.table)
library(jsonlite)
library(knitr)
library(digest)
library(readr)
show_table <- function(x) knitr::kable(x, format = "html", row.names = FALSE, escape = TRUE)
out <- "../artifacts/feature-preparation"
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
input <- "../artifacts/two-route-delivery-2026-10-01/route-b-api/openalex-route-b-api-2026-10-01-journals.csv.gz"
sha <- digest(input, algo = "sha256", file = TRUE)
stopifnot(sha == "46376a4fb026936c221c466ecf0fd3c2ab373eed1722ed7bad69a88ca4715724")
header <- names(read_csv(I(readLines(gzfile(input), n = 1L)), n_max = 0L,
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character(), show_col_types = FALSE))
labels <- read.csv("agreed-variable-labels.csv", check.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(length(header) == 80L, identical(header, labels[[1]]),
          sum(labels[[3]] == "yes") == 40L,
          all(labels[[3]][grepl("^scopus_.*_in_reference$", labels[[1]])] == "yes"))
fields <- c("route_row_id", "source_id", "display_name", "alternate_titles", "apc_prices",
  "apc_usd", "apc_usd_by_year", "language_works_count", "language_known_works_count",
  "language_unknown_works_count", "language_unknown_share", "language_counts_json",
  "language_proportions_json", "language_known_proportions_json", "issn", "issn_l",
  "type", "is_preprint_repository", "homepage_url", "created_date", "first_publication_year", "last_publication_year",
  "is_high_oa_rate_since_year", "is_in_doaj_since_year", "oa_flip_year")
# readr decodes doubled CSV quotes before the embedded JSON is parsed.
d <- read_csv(input, col_select = all_of(fields),
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character(),
  show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(problems(d)) == 0L)
setDT(d)
stopifnot(nrow(d) == 207602L, !anyDuplicated(d$route_row_id))
n <- nrow(d)
is_missing <- function(x) x %in% c("\\N", "\\M", "")
number <- function(x) as.numeric(replace(x, is_missing(x), NA_character_))
parse <- function(x) {
  if (is_missing(x)) return(NULL)
  fromJSON(x, simplifyVector = FALSE)
}
coverage <- function(field) {
  x <- d[[field]]
  data.frame(Field = field, Missing = sum(is_missing(x)),
    Empty_container = sum(x %in% c("[]", "{}")),
    Populated = sum(!is_missing(x) & !x %in% c("[]", "{}")))
}
count_table <- function(x, name) {
  z <- as.data.frame(table(x), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(z) <- c(name, "Sources")
  z
}
```

**Result:** The file hash, 80-column order, 40 yes / 40 no labels and unique row identities pass the checks above. `\N` means null, `\M` means an absent field, and `[]` / `{}` mean returned empty containers. Zero remains a value.

## 2. Are APC amounts already in dollars, and does the original currency list add anything?

**Answer:** `apc_usd` is a USD list price; `apc_prices` retains currency-labelled quotes. USD is present for **15,178 sources (7.31%)**. The original-price list adds **251 sources without a USD value**, so it should remain available for checking. Missing prices do not mean free publication; 660 sources explicitly record USD 0.


```{r}
#| label: apc-coverage
show_table(do.call(rbind, lapply(c("apc_prices", "apc_usd", "apc_usd_by_year"), coverage)))
prices <- lapply(d$apc_prices, parse)
history <- lapply(d$apc_usd_by_year, parse)
price_rows <- rbindlist(lapply(which(lengths(prices) > 0L), function(i) {
  rbindlist(lapply(prices[[i]], function(p) data.table(row = i, currency = p$currency, price = p$price)))
}))
history_rows <- rbindlist(lapply(which(lengths(history) > 0L), function(i) {
  rbindlist(lapply(history[[i]], function(p) data.table(row = i, year = p$year, price = p$price)))
}))
usd <- number(d$apc_usd)
apc_summary <- data.frame(
  Check = c("Original prices present, USD missing", "USD equals zero", "USD is positive",
    "Annual prices present", "More than one currency", "Duplicate years within a source",
    "USD present, original prices absent"),
  Sources = c(sum(lengths(prices) > 0L & is.na(usd)), sum(usd == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(usd > 0, na.rm = TRUE), sum(lengths(history) > 0L),
    price_rows[, uniqueN(currency), by = row][V1 > 1L, .N],
    history_rows[, anyDuplicated(year) > 0L, by = row][V1 == TRUE, .N],
    sum(!is.na(usd) & lengths(prices) == 0L)))
show_table(apc_summary)
missing_usd_prices <- price_rows[is.na(usd[row])]
stopifnot(!any(missing_usd_prices$currency == "USD"))
show_table(missing_usd_prices[, .(Sources_without_USD = uniqueN(row)),
  by = .(Original_currency = currency)][order(-Sources_without_USD)])
example <- which(d$source_id == "https://openalex.org/S107737141")
if (!length(example)) example <- which(d$source_id == "S107737141")
stopifnot(length(example) == 1L)
show_table(data.frame(Field = c("display_name", "apc_prices", "apc_usd", "apc_usd_by_year"),
  Value = vapply(c("display_name", "apc_prices", "apc_usd", "apc_usd_by_year"),
    function(k) d[[k]][example], character(1))))
```

**Result:** The 251 additional sources use 19 currencies, mainly Ukrainian hryvnia (115 sources) and Iranian rial (49). None has an explicit USD quote to copy across. Currency counts can overlap when a source lists several quotes. The Journal of Communication example shows how the three fields overlap. These are advertised charges, not payments by authors.

The [pre-freeze APC import code](https://github.com/ourresearch/openalex-sources/blob/ec51507ab4cb5ca917b9c0de2351252c478d1434/jobs/butler_apc.py) uses the dataset's USD values and refreshes original-currency quotes for recent covered journals. Other registry values can remain older. This explains why the three fields are not interchangeable. The export has no quote-level conversion date for the 251 USD-missing cases: retain their currency and amount, and leave USD missing rather than apply today's exchange rate to an undated quote.

## 3. Where do annual APCs come from, and which years are available?

**Answer:** The documented upstream route is the **Butler / ScholCommLab APC datasets**, including the 2019–2025 release. Our data contain annual prices for **12,407 sources (5.98%)**, covering **2019–2025**. Missing years were not filled by that importer; a blank year is not a zero charge.

```{r}
#| label: annual-apc-check
stopifnot(setequal(history_rows$year, 2019:2025))
show_table(history_rows[, .(Sources = uniqueN(row),
  Percent_of_cohort = round(100 * uniqueN(row) / n, 2)), by = year][order(year)])
latest <- history_rows[order(year), .SD[.N], by = row]
show_table(data.frame(Check = c("Current USD equals latest observed annual price",
  "Current USD differs from latest observed annual price", "Annual history present, current USD missing"),
  Sources = c(sum(usd[latest$row] == latest$price, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(usd[latest$row] != latest$price, na.rm = TRUE), sum(is.na(usd[latest$row])))))
```

**Result:** Annual coverage rises from 7,422 sources in 2019 to 11,230 in 2025, but the source composition changes. A trend in these cross-sectional averages would not establish price growth within journals.

The [importer](https://github.com/ourresearch/openalex-sources/blob/ec51507ab4cb5ca917b9c0de2351252c478d1434/jobs/butler_apc.py) keeps observed years only and updates current prices only when the latest observation is sufficiently recent. It takes converted USD from the input dataset; it does not perform a fresh exchange-rate conversion for these priced rows. The code identifies the import method, but our export does not contain a per-record import receipt. Use recorded yearly USD for the matching year, preserve gaps, and do not label the series inflation-adjusted or transaction prices.

## 4. Does `alternate_titles` mean abbreviations, and how should it be counted?

**Answer:** It contains alternative or former names, sometimes abbreviations. Count distinct returned names as `alternate_title_count`; do not call it an abbreviation count. If the main title is included, deduplicate it before counting total names. An empty list means no alternative name was returned.


```{r}
#| label: title-counts
titles <- lapply(d$alternate_titles, parse)
title_n <- lengths(titles)
title_unique_n <- vapply(titles, function(x) length(unique(unlist(x))), integer(1))
title_matches_main <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) d$display_name[i] %in% unlist(titles[[i]]), logical(1))
show_table(count_table(title_n, "Alternative_title_entries"))
show_table(data.frame(Check = c("Exact duplicates within the list", "List contains the exact main title"),
  Sources = c(sum(title_n != title_unique_n), sum(title_matches_main))))
title_case <- which(title_n > 0L)[1:3]
show_table(data.frame(Source = d$display_name[title_case], List = d$alternate_titles[title_case],
                 Entries = title_n[title_case]))
```

**Result:** `r sum(title_matches_main)` lists already contain the exact main title, and `r sum(title_n != title_unique_n)` contain exact duplicates. Adding one to every list length would overcount some sources. [OpenAlex distinguishes alternative titles from its separate abbreviation field](https://help.openalex.org/data/sources/attributes/); the list has no dates with which to reconstruct name changes.

## 5. What is the denominator of each language share?

**Answer:** `language_proportions_json` divides each language count by **all counted works, including unknown language**. `language_known_proportions_json` divides by known-language works only. The agreed version is the first. For the 11,392 sources with no counted works, shares are undefined, not zero.


```{r}
#| label: language-denominators
total <- number(d$language_works_count)
known <- number(d$language_known_works_count)
unknown <- number(d$language_unknown_works_count)
unknown_share <- number(d$language_unknown_share)
counts <- lapply(d$language_counts_json, parse)
shares <- lapply(d$language_proportions_json, parse)
known_shares <- lapply(d$language_known_proportions_json, parse)
positive <- which(total > 0)
language_errors <- vapply(positive, function(i) {
  cts <- unlist(counts[[i]])
  ps <- unlist(shares[[i]])
  ks <- unlist(known_shares[[i]])
  known_cts <- cts[names(cts) != "__unknown__"]
  expected_unknown <- if ("__unknown__" %in% names(cts)) cts[["__unknown__"]] else 0
  max(c(abs(sum(cts) - total[i]), abs(expected_unknown - unknown[i]),
    abs(known[i] + unknown[i] - total[i]), abs(sum(ps) - 1),
    abs(ps - cts[names(ps)] / total[i]), abs(unknown_share[i] - unknown[i] / total[i]),
    if (known[i] > 0) abs(ks - known_cts[names(ks)] / known[i]) else length(ks)))
}, numeric(1))
stopifnot(all(is.finite(language_errors)), max(language_errors) < 1e-9,
  all(vapply(positive, function(i) setequal(names(counts[[i]]), names(shares[[i]])), logical(1))),
  all(vapply(positive, function(i) setequal(setdiff(names(counts[[i]]), "__unknown__"),
    names(known_shares[[i]])), logical(1))),
  all(lengths(counts)[total == 0] == 0L), all(lengths(shares)[total == 0] == 0L),
  all(is.na(unknown_share[total == 0])))
language_codes <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(counts, names))))
show_table(data.frame(Check = c("Zero denominator: shares undefined", "Positive denominator", "At least one unknown-language work", "All works have unknown language"),
  Sources = c(sum(total == 0), sum(total > 0), sum(unknown > 0), sum(total > 0 & known == 0))))
language_rows <- rbindlist(lapply(positive, function(i) {
  data.table(row = i, code = names(counts[[i]]), count = as.numeric(unlist(counts[[i]])))
}))
language_totals <- language_rows[, .(Sources = uniqueN(row), Works = sum(count)),
  by = .(Code = code)][order(-Works)]
non_two_letter_codes <- setdiff(language_codes[!grepl("^[a-z]{2}$", language_codes)], "__unknown__")
code_anomaly_journals <- language_rows[code %in% non_two_letter_codes, uniqueN(row)]
lang_case <- which(unknown > 0 & known > 0)[1]
show_table(data.frame(Field = c("display_name", "language_works_count", "language_known_works_count",
  "language_unknown_works_count", "language_counts_json", "language_proportions_json",
  "language_known_proportions_json", "language_unknown_share"),
  Value = vapply(c("display_name", "language_works_count", "language_known_works_count",
    "language_unknown_works_count", "language_counts_json", "language_proportions_json",
    "language_known_proportions_json", "language_unknown_share"), function(k) d[[k]][lang_case], character(1))))
```

**Result:** Counts, totals and both share definitions agree for every source with works; the maximum numerical error is `r format(max(language_errors), scientific=TRUE)`. These are counts of works assigned to each source, not editorial language policies or confirmed full-text languages.

## 6. Are unknown-language counts and shares perfectly correlated?

**Answer:** No. The Pearson correlation is **0.117** across sources with works. Counts measure volume; shares measure the fraction with unknown language. The exact duplicate is `language_unknown_share` and the `__unknown__` entry in the all-work share dictionary.

```{r}
#| label: unknown-language-correlation
unknown_correlation <- cor(unknown[positive], unknown_share[positive], method = "pearson")
unknown_dictionary_share <- vapply(positive, function(i) {
  if (is.null(shares[[i]][["__unknown__"]])) return(0)
  shares[[i]][["__unknown__"]]
}, numeric(1))
show_table(data.frame(Sources = length(positive), Pearson_r = unknown_correlation,
  Maximum_duplicate_difference = max(abs(unknown_dictionary_share - unknown_share[positive]))))
```

**Result:** Keep unknown share once when expanding the dictionary. The low count–share correlation corrects the untested claim in the discussion; it does not by itself establish which field improves a model.

## 7. Are all language codes already standardized?

**Answer:** No. There are **`r length(setdiff(language_codes, "__unknown__"))` non-unknown labels**, including 79 that are not two lowercase letters, affecting 10,814 sources. They include valid longer language codes as well as aliases and miscellaneous labels. This is mixed upstream metadata, not evidence that all 79 are invalid languages. Keep the original codes; map verified aliases before expanding them into model columns.

```{r}
#| label: language-code-check
show_table(data.frame(Non_unknown_labels = length(setdiff(language_codes, "__unknown__")),
  Non_two_letter_labels = length(non_two_letter_codes), Affected_sources = code_anomaly_journals))
show_table(language_totals[Code %in% c("en", "eng", "英语", "영어", "zh", "zh-cn", "zh-tw", "中文", "other")])
```

**Result:** [The local import](https://github.com/YannJY02/InvisibleResearch/blob/main/research/openalex-journal-baseline/analysis/build_dual_route_datasets.py) preserves API language groups, lowercases their labels and combines `unknown` / `null` into `__unknown__`. It does not generate `eng`, `zh-cn` or Chinese-language labels. [Current OpenAlex guidance](https://help.openalex.org/data/languages/) describes title/abstract language inference and two-letter codes; the frozen values show that this description is not a complete validation rule. Keep dialect distinctions and unresolved labels separate rather than silently convert everything to English, Chinese or unknown.

show_table(language_totals)

## 8. Why are 19 preprint sources present in a journal dataset?

**Answer:** They were already labelled **`type=journal` and `is_preprint_repository=true` in the original OpenAlex responses**. Our journal filter used the first field; it did not exclude the second. Upstream stores and exports the two fields independently. This is inherited source classification, not a join error introduced by this project.

The labels also describe different publishing arrangements: [Preprints.org](https://www.preprints.org/about) hosts unreviewed manuscripts, whereas [Qeios](https://www.qeios.com/publishing-policy) publishes preprints and peer-approved journal articles. Treating every flagged source as the same kind of mistake would lose this distinction. **Retain the 19 records and their flag in the agreed OpenAlex-defined cohort; report a sensitivity analysis excluding them if the study claims to describe conventional journals.** No rows are deleted here.

```{r}
#| label: preprint-original-response-check
# Re-read the frozen raw responses, not today's API. Python streams the large
# JSONL file; the report compares its result with the R-loaded analysis table.
probe <- '
import gzip, json, sys
selected = []
rows = 0
with gzip.open(sys.argv[1], "rt") as stream:
    for line in stream:
        rec = json.loads(line)
        obj = rec["source"]
        rows += 1
        if obj.get("is_preprint_repository"):
            selected.append({"source_id": obj["id"].split("/")[-1],
                "type": obj["type"], "preprint": obj["is_preprint_repository"],
                "fetched_at": rec["fetched_at"]})
with open(sys.argv[2], "w") as stream:
    json.dump({"rows": rows, "records": selected}, stream)
'
probe_file <- file.path(out, "verify-raw-preprints.py")
raw_check_file <- file.path(out, "raw-preprint-check.json")
writeLines(probe, probe_file)
stopifnot(system2("python3", c(shQuote(probe_file),
  shQuote("../artifacts/two-route-current-api-2026-10-01/sources.jsonl.gz"),
  shQuote(raw_check_file))) == 0L)
raw_check <- fromJSON(raw_check_file)
stopifnot(all(grepl("^2026-10-01", raw_check$records$fetched_at)))
preprints <- d[tolower(is_preprint_repository) == "true"]
stopifnot(raw_check$rows == n, nrow(preprints) == 19L,
  all(raw_check$records$type == "journal"), all(raw_check$records$preprint),
  setequal(sub(".*/", "", preprints$source_id), raw_check$records$source_id),
  all(preprints$type == "journal"))
show_table(preprints[, .(Source = display_name, Source_ID = source_id, ISSNs = issn)])
```

**Result:** All 19 flags agree with the original responses collected on 1 October. The [upstream source snapshot](https://github.com/ourresearch/openalex-walden/blob/7021748a6946c262484437b356f355d2b9e1a494/notebooks/sources/CreateSources.ipynb) passes through both registry fields, and its [API builder](https://github.com/ourresearch/openalex-walden/blob/7021748a6946c262484437b356f355d2b9e1a494/notebooks/sources/CreateSourcesApi.ipynb) exports them separately. That establishes the origin of the coexistence; it does not certify every historical classification decision. The cohort is therefore accurately described as *OpenAlex sources classified as journals*, not a verified census of peer-reviewed journals.

## 9. Can ISSNs be counted, and does ISSN-L identify print or electronic editions?

**Answer:** Count distinct ISSNs in the returned list. **Do not add ISSN-L as another edition:** it is a linking identifier selected from the ISSNs. The arrays have no print/electronic labels, so their order cannot identify the medium. A missing list is unknown, not a confirmed count of zero.


```{r}
#| label: issn-counts
issns <- lapply(d$issn, parse)
issn_n <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
  if (is_missing(d$issn[i])) return(NA_integer_)
  length(unique(unlist(issns[[i]])))
}, integer(1))
issn_check <- function(x) {
  if (!grepl("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{3}[0-9X]$", x)) return(FALSE)
  chars <- strsplit(gsub("-", "", x), "")[[1]]
  digits <- as.numeric(replace(chars, chars == "X", "10"))
  sum(digits * 8:1) %% 11 == 0
}
issn_tokens <- unique(unlist(issns))
issn_valid <- vapply(issn_tokens, issn_check, logical(1))
invalid_issns <- issn_tokens[!issn_valid]
l_present <- !is_missing(d$issn_l)
l_in_list <- vapply(which(l_present), function(i) d$issn_l[i] %in% unlist(issns[[i]]), logical(1))
show_table(count_table(ifelse(is.na(issn_n), "Missing", as.character(issn_n)), "Distinct_ISSNs"))
show_table(data.frame(Check = c("ISSN-L present", "ISSN-L already in the ISSN list",
  "ISSN-L present, ISSN list missing", "Both present, ISSN-L absent from list",
  "At least one invalid ISSN format or checksum"),
  Sources = c(sum(l_present), sum(l_in_list), sum(l_present & is.na(issn_n)),
    sum(l_present & !is.na(issn_n)) - sum(l_in_list),
    sum(vapply(issns, function(x) any(unlist(x) %in% invalid_issns), logical(1))))))
show_table(data.frame(Source = d$display_name[example], issn = d$issn[example], issn_l = d$issn_l[example]))
```

**Result:** The largest returned list has `r max(issn_n, na.rm=TRUE)` distinct ISSNs, so the suggested 0/1/2 categories are insufficient. [The ISSN International Centre](https://www.issn.org/understanding-the-issn/assignment-rules/the-issn-l-for-publications-on-multiple-media/) defines ISSN-L as a link across media. Use a distinct-count feature with missingness retained; separate print/electronic indicators require medium-labelled records. Checksum validity alone does not verify a journal–identifier match.

## 10. What do the years mean, and how should missing or suspicious values be handled?

**Answer:** First/last publication years describe indexed works, not a verified journal lifespan. Missing OA years do not mean “never OA.” Use missing values as missing, and do not calculate age from year 0. Two specific values need interpretation: Kew's first year 0 is unusable, while the high-OA year 2027 can reflect an upstream year-offset convention rather than an announced future launch.


```{r}
#| label: year-coverage
year_fields <- c("first_publication_year", "last_publication_year",
  "is_high_oa_rate_since_year", "is_in_doaj_since_year", "oa_flip_year")
year_summary <- rbindlist(lapply(year_fields, function(k) {
  x <- number(d[[k]])
  data.table(Field = k, Present = sum(!is.na(x)), Missing = sum(is.na(x)), Zero = sum(x == 0, na.rm=TRUE),
    Minimum = min(x, na.rm=TRUE), Maximum = max(x, na.rm=TRUE),
    After_2026 = sum(x > 2026, na.rm=TRUE))
}))
show_table(year_summary)
show_table(coverage("created_date"))
first <- number(d$first_publication_year)
last <- number(d$last_publication_year)
show_table(data.frame(Check = c("First year after last year", "At least one DOAJ or high-OA year present"),
  Sources = c(sum(first > last, na.rm=TRUE), sum(!is_missing(d$is_in_doaj_since_year) |
    !is_missing(d$is_high_oa_rate_since_year)))))
year_anomalies <- rbindlist(lapply(year_fields, function(k) {
  rows <- which(!is.na(number(d[[k]])) & (number(d[[k]]) <= 0 | number(d[[k]]) > 2026))
  data.table(Source = d$display_name[rows], Source_ID = d$source_id[rows], Field = rep(k, length(rows)), Value = d[[k]][rows])
}))
show_table(year_anomalies)
```

**Result:** Kew's historical bulletin began in **1887**, as documented by [Kew's own historical account](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12225-025-10301-z). This establishes that 0 is not its founding year; it does not justify silently replacing a field defined as the earliest indexed work with a founding date. Keep 0 in the raw data and mark the analysis value missing.

For *Digestive and Liver Disease*, the frozen record contains high-OA year **2027** and `oa_flip_year=2026`. The [registry code](https://github.com/ourresearch/openalex-sources/blob/ec51507ab4cb5ca917b9c0de2351252c478d1434/jobs/apply_oa_flags.py) can store a curated flip year plus one as the high-OA year; the [API calculation](https://github.com/ourresearch/openalex-walden/blob/7021748a6946c262484437b356f355d2b9e1a494/notebooks/sources/CreateSourcesApi.ipynb) subtracts one again. This is an observed pair consistent with that convention, not proof of the private curation entry. The [publisher currently identifies the journal as open access](https://www.dldjournalonline.com/). Do not describe 2027 as a verified future transition or treat it as a completed event at the 2026 freeze.

The same API code aggregates cumulative citations by the works' publication year and derives `created_date` from associated work records, whereas [current documentation](https://help.openalex.org/data/common-attributes/) describes these dates differently. Use neutral field labels and the frozen values; neither `created_date` nor first indexed publication establishes journal age. Historical prediction requires predictor values actually available at its observation date.

## 11. What can be encoded next, and where does BERTopic fit?

**Answer:** The checks support counts for returned names/ISSNs, language shares with unknown represented once, and year-specific USD prices with gaps retained. Title words, homepage presence and identifier presence remain simple candidates. BERTopic is a separate text-analysis option; it does not convert the existing OpenAlex topic IDs into meaningful numbers.

| Information retained in the discussion | Supported next representation |
|---|---|
| Alternative names / ISSNs | Distinct returned count; preserve missing ISSN lists |
| Language | Verified code mapping, then all-work shares; one unknown-share column |
| APC | USD for the relevant year, with missingness; original currency for checks |
| Main title / homepage / Wikidata | Declared title-word indicators or text features; presence indicators; publisher identity requires a verified match |
| Preprint flag | Retain; compare results with and without the 19 flagged sources |
| Dates and OA years | Keep distinct meanings; invalid analysis values missing; no future information |
| Existing topic classifications | Categorical indicators or shares at an explicitly selected hierarchy level |

[BERTopic's original method](https://maartengr.github.io/BERTopic/algorithm/algorithm.html) combines text embeddings, dimensionality reduction, clustering and topic-word representations. A journal-level study would need a stated corpus, such as article titles/abstracts, followed by aggregation to journals. Journal names alone are not an adequate substitute for that corpus. No topic model was run for this field check.

These are evidence-backed recommendations, not new shared decisions. The next implementation needs the study's outcome and observation date to be selected; then missing-value treatment and feature selection must be fitted within training data, following the [official guidance on data leakage](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html#data-leakage).
